sections.title: How does the AP® chem score calculator work?
sections.html:
The AP® chem score calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports composite score (0-100) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the long question 1 (0-10), the long question 2 (0-10), the long question 3 (0-10) and the short question 1 (0-4).

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Multiple-choice (0-60) = 10, Long question 1 (0-10) = 10, Long question 2 (0-10) = 10 and Long question 3 (0-10) = 10. Working through the relationship above gives Composite score (0-100) = 84 and AP® score (1-5) = 5.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Composite score (0-100) = 84 and AP® score (1-5) = 5 should be roughly the size you expected from Multiple-choice (0-60) = 10 and Long question 1 (0-10) = 10.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The AP® chem score calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the long question 1, the long question 2 and the long question 3 — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

faq.q: What does the AP® chem score calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns composite score (0-100), derived from the long question 1, the long question 2 and the long question 3. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the AP® chem score calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the long question 1, the long question 2, the long question 3 and the short question 1, which is 8 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Composite score (0-100) = 84. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the AP® chem score calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. The calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
